title: Glass Jobs Held by One Customer (Auto Glass Services)
content:
**Auto Glass Services — desk guidance on the number of glass jobs held by one customer.**

> A customer may hold any number of glass jobs across vehicles; there is no customer-level cap. Per vehicle, the rule limiting the open glass jobs one vehicle may have applies.

## What the rule fixes

| Level | Limit set by this rule |
|---|---|
| The customer, across all of the customer's vehicles | None — no maximum number of glass jobs per customer is set |
| One vehicle | Not set here; the per-vehicle limit on open glass jobs governs each vehicle |

## Points of judgement

- The count of glass jobs a customer already holds on other vehicles is not, under this rule, a reason to decline a glass job on a further vehicle.
- The rule counts nothing at the customer level, so there is no customer-level figure to compare against: any number of jobs across vehicles is within it.
- Whatever the customer's total, each vehicle is judged separately under the per-vehicle rule.

## Hypothetical illustration

A fleet account (hypothetical) runs five vans, each needing glass work at the same time. Under this rule, the five glass jobs, one on each van, raise no customer-level limit, because none exists; each van is then looked at on its own under the per-vehicle rule.
